name: ceo-of-second-hand/air-raid-alerts-forecast (Air Raid Alerts in Ukraine - Time Series Forecasting)
authors: [uncertain] GitHub user ceo-of-second-hand; the README/DECISIONS refer to the human author as Ivanka, working with Claude Code (commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude)
popularity: 0 stars, no forks; no license file (licenseInfo null) as of 2026-10-17
peer_review_status: student repo, self-reported claims; not peer-reviewed. We re-checked some numbers from the committed reports/final_predictions.csv.
target_type: Onset-style (an alert start), but NOT at-risk masked: any raion- or oblast-level alert start in the window counts, including starts while the oblast is already under alert. So it sits between onset and state. Base rates are very high (3h: 0.37 pooled, 0.87 Kharkivska, 0.84 Dnipropetrovska, 0.82 Sumska), so frontline scores partly reflect the high activity level.
target_definition: y_h(T) = 1 if at least one raion- or oblast-level alert row in oblast r starts in the hourly bins [T, T+h), where T = start of the hour and starts are floored to the hour. Main horizon h = 3 h; 1 h and 6 h also reported. A new forecast every hour. Hromada-level rows are excluded from events (mostly strike-drone threat posts). The target was chosen over daily counts and duration in d2_target_comparison.py, which scored the test period.
spatial_unit: oblast (24 units = 23 oblasts + Kyiv City; Luhanska and Crimea/Sevastopol excluded)
at_risk_masking: No. Every hour of every oblast is trained on and scored ('every hour', 24,120 rows at 3 h in the test). Rows already under alert are not excluded. The 'active_at_T' feature was dropped as leaky (L37), so the model does not even know whether the oblast is under alert. This differs from our CLAUDE.md target rule (mask rows already under alert).
data_sources: Vadimkin/ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset official_data_en.csv (MIT; parsed from the @air_alert_ua Telegram channel), downloaded from a pinned upstream commit with SHA-256 checks. Window used: 2025-12-01 to 2026-09-06 21:00 UTC (about 9 months, the raion-level era); 7-day feature warm-up drops 1-7 Dec. Volunteer CSV used only for a cross-check (D1); alerts.in.ua API not used (future work). District boundaries from the dataset repo's ukr_admin2.geojson were used to build oblast adjacency.
data_source_variant: Official file only. Admin levels: union of raion + oblast rows per oblast (hromada rows dropped; no interval union because only starts are used). Snapshot: official file frozen at 2026-09-07; cut at 2026-09-06 21:00 UTC (midnight Kyiv). Training restricted to post-Dec-2025 to avoid the raion-reform definition change.
preprocessing: Exact duplicate rows dropped (about 38% of official rows), Luhansk/Crimea/Sevastopol excluded with a test, hromada level dropped, starts floored to hourly bins. No standing-alert rule: 623 alerts over 24 h left as-is (L34), which no longer matters once only start times are used. No handling of the 2026-08-30 to 09-01 recording gap: those hours are kept and scored as 'no alert start' (we checked: 0 positive labels on 30 Aug, 31 Aug and 1 Sep in final_predictions.csv, and 51/576 on 29 Aug).
known_label_artefacts: Documented: (1) 38% exact duplicates, removed. (2) 623 alerts lasting over 24 h (possibly missed all-clears, e.g. Synelnykivskyi raion up to 115 h), left as-is, made irrelevant by using start times only. (3) The parser closes a missing all-clear at start + 1 h without a flag when a new start comes more than 3 h later, and overwrites the first start when the new alert comes within 3 h. So some starts are lost. Listed as a limitation; cannot be fixed from the CSV. (4) Volunteer parser mis-assigns about 1/30 messages to the wrong oblast (Podilskyi -> Lviv, Prylutskyi -> Volyn). They found this by replaying the parser and rejected the volunteer file. (5) Alerts still open when the channel stopped (2026-09-07 06:09 UTC) are never written. Not handled: the 30 Aug to 1 Sep recording gap is treated as true zeros, not masked. Not discussed: exactly-30-min durations (irrelevant to start-only features).
model_family: sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier (max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, region_code as categorical, seed 0), not tuned, no early stopping. Logistic regression (one-hot oblast/hour/weekday, log1p counts, scaling inside each fold) compared and rejected by a pre-registered rule (L27: prefer LR unless GBM beats it by more than 1 pp of skill). Separate models per horizon.
features: Final set (start times only, L37): region_code (categorical); own alert starts in previous 1/3/6/24/168 h (windows end strictly before T); national starts in previous 1 h and 3 h; neighbour-oblast starts in previous 1 h and 3 h (adjacency computed from raion polygons by build_adjacency.py); Kyiv-local hour of day and weekday. Dropped: active_at_T and nb_active (alerts active now, own and neighbours), because the official parser fills missing end times using later starts. They cost +4.6% Brier at 3 h in validation. Dropped by reasoning: distance to border/occupied territory (fixed per oblast, so it adds nothing beyond oblast identity). No time-since-last-start/end features. No external features.
external_feature_timing: Not applicable: no external features. Weather explicitly rejected because only forecast weather at T would be leak-free and they had no archive of forecasts. Telegram launch reports listed as future work with the publication-before-T rule (L8).
ablation_design: Yes, on the same rows. D7/D8: four variants (LR/GBM x with/without neighbours) trained on identical rows in each of the same 10 walk-forward folds, rules fixed before running (neighbours kept if they improve Brier in >= 8/10 folds; GBM only if it beats LR by more than 1 pp). Neighbours improved both models in 9/10 folds (+1.3% LR, +1.6% GBM). The end-time-feature ablation (L37) also used the same 10 folds and was adopted 'whatever it scores'.
split_scheme: Chronological. Walk-forward on pre-test data: 10 folds of 2 weeks each (2026-03-08 to 2026-07-26), expanding window starting 2025-12-01, minimum 12 weeks of training (first fold has 14). They planned 11 folds, an arithmetic error they disclosed. Purged by h at each cut-off, baselines refitted per fold. Final: train on everything before 2026-07-26 21:00 UTC minus h, test = last 6 weeks 2026-07-26 21:00 to 2026-09-06 21:00 UTC. No refit inside the test. No separate validation slice for early stopping (none used).
metrics: Primary: Brier skill score vs the best start-only recency rule (chosen on validation). Secondary: skill vs climatology, Brier, ROC-AUC pooled AND mean within-oblast, log-loss, accuracy@0.5 next to majority-class accuracy, calibration table and plot, weekly and per-oblast breakdowns, fold-win counts with a sign test. No PR-AUC.
unit_of_metric: Both: pooled AUC (0.907 at 3 h) and mean per-oblast AUC (0.699). They explicitly call pooled AUC inflated by between-oblast differences and say it is not a headline number.
baseline_strength: Climatology: oblast x hour x weekday rate from train. Recency rule: a lookup P(y | oblast, any start in the last k h) fitted on train and frozen (not rolling). k picked on validation from 1/3/6 h (1h->k=3, 3h->k=6, 6h->k=6). An earlier '3h + active' variant was dropped as leaky. Hard 0/1 persistence shown only as a warning example (-63% skill). No calibrated persistence under that name, though the recency lookup is close to it. Test skill at 3 h: +10.4% vs recency, +19.2% vs climatology. Validation mean at 3 h with the final features: +3.0% vs recency, 10/10 folds.
calibration: No calibration fitted (raw GBM probabilities). Test reliability table in 10 bins plus calibration_test.png and calibration_dryrun.png. The test calibration is close to the diagonal (for example, predicted 0.036 vs observed 0.027; 0.748 vs 0.802; 0.951 vs 0.951). They slightly over-predict in the lowest bins and under-predict at 0.5-0.8.
calibration_under_drift: No explicit calibration-in-the-large test vs validation and no recalibration. They do report the base rate per split (3 h test base rate 0.369). The validation-vs-test gap in skill (+3.0% vs +10.4%) is discussed. They do not check the new yellow/red regime after 2026-09-07 at all.
uncertainty_of_gain: No CI or DM test. Uncertainty is shown by fold/week counts: 10/10 validation folds won (sign test p = 0.001 claimed; they note it is approximate because neighbouring folds are correlated), 6/6 test weeks won, and the min/max fold skill (+0.7% to +9.3% in the earlier walk-forward). They state that a realistic gain lies between the validation +3.0% and the test +10.4%.
regime_coverage: Narrow. Only post-Dec-2025 (raion-level) data, so the Dec-2025 raion reform is avoided rather than spanned, and the Jan-2025 drone surge is outside the data. The Sep-2026 yellow/red regime is not evaluated (data ends 2026-09-06). Listed as future work: alerts.in.ua API as a prospective test.
leakage_handling: Strong for a 1-day project. (1) All counts use starts strictly before T (shift(1)). (2) Purging: training rows with hour < cutoff - h, asserted in code and in a pytest test over every fold, the dry run and the final split. (3) Truncation test: delete every alert starting at or after T0 and push later end times later, then check features at hours <= T0 are unchanged. No negative control (no deliberately leaky feature that the test must catch). (4) An independent review (H1) found that end-time features leak because the official parser imputes missing ends from future starts, so active_at_T/nb_active were removed and the recency opponent was made start-only too. Climatology and lookups are fitted on train only, and the LR scaler is fitted inside the pipeline. Missed: the recording gap is scored as true zeros (a data-validity problem, not a leak, but it inflates the result; see headline_results). Also, the hour-floored label [T, T+h) and features from bins < T are consistent, but there is no masking for the oblast already being under alert.
test_window_hygiene: Weak by their own disclosure. The test period was looked at 3 times before the final run: #1 target selection (d2_target_comparison.py scored the test, and the 3 h target was chosen with test results), #2 adding recency baselines on test (+9%), and #4 a re-run for report text. Then the final run #8, with a lock file reports/.test_scored and a --rerun-reason guard. experiments.md logs every look. Model choice, features and the recency k were frozen on validation before #8, and the #8 log entry was written before metrics were computed. d2 script now refuses to run without --i-know-this-scores-the-test-period.
headline_results: Test (2026-07-26 to 2026-09-06, 24 oblasts, every hour), reported: 3 h Brier 0.1185 vs recency(k=6h) 0.1322 vs climatology 0.1467, so skill +10.4% vs recency and +19.2% vs climatology, better in 6/6 weeks (weekly skill +3.5%, +8.0%, +5.2%, +4.7%, +12.1%, +26.4%). 1 h: +5.8% vs recency (Brier 0.1116 vs 0.1185). 6 h: +6.1%. AUC 3 h pooled 0.907 vs recency 0.888; within-oblast mean 0.699 vs 0.630 (validation, 20 weeks: 0.659 vs recency 0.554 vs climatology 0.537; pooled 0.882). Log-loss 0.372 vs 0.407. Per oblast: the model loses to recency in 6 low-base-rate western oblasts (Lviv -17%, Ivano-Frankivsk -16%, Chernivtsi -15%, Zakarpattia -10%, Rivne -6%, Volyn -2%) and wins most in high-rate frontline ones (Dnipropetrovsk +32%, Sumy +30%, Kharkiv +22%). Validation (final features) 3 h: +3.0% vs recency, 10/10 folds. [uncertain: our re-check uses approximate gap edges 2026-08-29 18:00 to 2026-09-02 06:00 UTC, not exact detected edges] OUR RE-CHECK from final_predictions.csv: the 2026-08-30 to 09-01 recording gap (0 labels on those days) is in test week 6. Removing about 29 Aug 18:00 to 2 Sep 06:00 UTC (approximate edges; 2,016 rows) drops the 3 h skill vs recency from +10.4% to +5.8% (Brier 0.1253 vs 0.1330). On the gap rows alone the skill is +65%, because the model's features read the empty window as zero activity, while the frozen recency lookup is weaker there. Week 6 without the gap: +6.4% instead of +26%. So the honest test gain is about +6%, still above the validation +3.0%, and the model still beats recency.
code_available: Yes, public on GitHub, no license file. Python 3.12, pinned requirements (numpy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, shapely, matplotlib, pytest). Scripts chain-import each other (no shared module yet, so the final model depends on the frozen d2 script). Data downloaded by script from a pinned upstream commit with SHA-256 checks. Predictions CSV and reports committed. A one-day project, not maintained after 2026-10-12.
takeaways_for_project: 1) The recording gap really matters (supports our D-013 masking): in this peer's test, 3 unmasked gap days inflate the headline 3 h BSS from about +5.8% to +10.4% and week-6 skill from about +6% to +26%. We must keep masking the gap and features that read across it (D-013), and mention this peer result in the README as outside evidence. 2) Their lack of at-risk masking plus raion-level starts gives base rates of 0.8-0.9 in frontline oblasts. With our mask (D-020 causal rule) the base rates and skills are not comparable to theirs; compare only qualitatively. 3) The pooled vs within-oblast AUC gap (0.91 vs 0.70; validation 0.88 vs 0.66) matches our rule of reporting both. Expect within-oblast AUC around 0.65-0.70 to be a realistic range. 4) A frozen recency lookup is a weaker opponent than our rolling 14-day recency (D-021). Their +10% gain over a frozen lookup does not mean the same over our rolling, shrunken baseline. 5) Their L37 finding: official end times are imputed using future starts (missing all-clear closed at start + 1 h when the next start comes more than 3 h later). This is a concrete leakage risk for our minutes_since_last_end and active_at_t features. Our D-020 24h causal cap does not fix imputed ends, so we should check whether our end-time features carry this leak, or at least name it as a limitation. 6) Their validation-vs-test gap (+3.0% vs +10.4%) suggests reporting the validation skill next to the test skill, plus our week-block bootstrap CI (D-013), to avoid over-reading one 6-week window. 7) Western low-rate oblasts are where the GBM loses to recency. Expect the same in our rear group and report per group. 8) Their test was seen 3 times before the final run. Our protocol of scoring it once at M4 (CLAUDE.md) is stricter; keep the lock-file idea (a .test_scored guard with a --rerun-reason) as cheap hygiene.
best_practices: Adopt: a pre-registered decision rule before each experiment (fold-win thresholds, an LR-vs-GBM margin, 'adopt whatever it scores' for the leak fix); experiments.md logging every look at the test; a lock file plus a rerun-reason guard on the test-scoring script; a dry run of the final code path on the last validation fold that must reproduce the validation number exactly; making the baseline leak-free too when a leaky feature is removed from the model; reporting within-oblast AUC and calling pooled AUC inflated; per-oblast and per-week tables; replaying the upstream parser on raw channel messages to check label quality; data pinned to an upstream commit with SHA-256; disclosing arithmetic errors instead of fixing them silently. Avoid: choosing the target on the test period; scoring a recording gap as true zeros; no at-risk masking (it mixes 'already active' persistence with onset skill); a frozen rather than rolling recency opponent; a truncation test without a negative control; chained script imports instead of a shared module; a sign test on correlated folds presented with a precise p-value; no CI on the skill gain; and no check after the regime change.
